narrative.overview:
Picture the board at the nurses' station: color-coded, glanceable, no wasted words, built to be read correctly in the two seconds someone has between other tasks. That's the system. Every screen exists to answer one question fast — is this facility's vaccine stock fine, low, or critical — and everything else is the supporting record for that one glance.

The system uses the Clinical Material design language: warm paper surfaces, a forest-green sidebar, the Figtree Variable webfont, thin large greeting headers, and full dark mode support. It explicitly rejects the consumer/marketing-app register: no gradients, no playful illustration, no decorative motion.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper background (#F3F3F1 light / #171B18 dark), forest-green sidebar (#1D2721)
CSS variable design tokens (RGB channel triplets) — all colors route through tailwind.config.js token map
Full dark mode: manual toggle (TopBar Sun/Moon) + OS prefers-color-scheme auto (now enabled)
PageHeader component: thin 34–38px greeting title + breadcrumb, replaces old primary-color banner headers
Flat surfaces, 18px rounded cards (rounded-xl), 1px hairline borders (border-surface-border)
Status always paired with text label, never color alone; statusConfig() is the single source of truth

rules.name: The Status-Only Saturation Rule
rules.body: Saturated color means one of two things: an action (forest green) or a stock status (red/amber/green). Never use bright color for decoration.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode color values in component or page files. All colors come from Tailwind token classes (bg-surface, text-primary, border-surface-border, etc.) which map to CSS variables in index.css.

rules.name: The Border-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Every surface that's part of the page layout is flat with a hairline border at rest. Shadow only on the two floating elements (Modal, Toast).

rules.name: The statusConfig Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode status colors or labels. Always call statusConfig(status) from src/lib/status.js.

dos: Do treat the red/amber/green/no-data quartet as sacred — always paired with a text label, sourced from statusConfig().
Do keep every laid-out surface flat with a hairline border; reserve shadow for the two floating elements (Modal, Toast).
Do size touch targets generously on Facility Worker screens — used on a phone, often one-handed.
Do write error messages that state the current true value ("Only 12 left"), not just that something failed.
Do use PageHeader at the top of every page instead of a colored banner div.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, playful illustration, or decorative motion.
Don't let a static (non-clickable) card carry a shadow.
Don't hardcode bg-white, bg-slate-50, border-slate-200 — use bg-surface, bg-surface-alt, border-surface-border.
Don't use Recharts SVG attributes with CSS variables — use useTheme() to get concrete hex values.
